label: CAUSE_OF_BEING_1: originating cause of being, giving a thing being at a first moment of its presence
definition: OriginatesBeing h G v c x: for some moment b, x begins at b in history v (present at b and at no strictly earlier moment, TemporalHistory.BeginsAt) and c gives x being at b (BeingGiving.GivesAt). Nothing is required of c at later moments. Ordinary meaning: the cause from which a thing's being takes its start. Examples: the builder of a house, who gives the house its being as it comes to be and then stops (q.104 a.1 co.); a parent of a child. Counterexample: a thing with no first moment of presence (presence on an open interval of dense time) has no originating cause in this sense; a cause that acts on x only after x's first moment is not originating. Distinguished from CAUSE_OF_BEING_2 (sustaining), which requires giving at every moment at which x is present, and from the cause of coming to be anew (DEF-CAUSE-OF-ORIGIN, CausesOrigin), which is not time-indexed and not tied to giving being.
note: Analyst reading, attribution deferred: q.104 a.1's builder (cause of becoming whose ceasing does not end the house) motivates the time profile; no claim states it. Relation to the other sense: a sustaining cause of a thing with a first moment of presence is an originating cause of it (originatesOfSustains, a helper lemma in the SustainingCausation Solution); the converse fails (SustainingCausation Control.inertia). Structural properties: none built in. It is the sense an existential-inertia theorist (Schmid 2021) can grant for every caused thing.
